definitions.signature: static func _polar(bearing: float, radius: float, y: float) -> Vector3:
definitions.formula: angle = deg_to_rad(bearing); return Vector3(sin(angle) * radius, y, cos(angle) * radius)

definitions.signature: static func _polar(bearing: float, radius: float, y: float) -> Vector3:
definitions.formula: angle = deg_to_rad(bearing); return Vector3(sin(angle) * radius, y, cos(angle) * radius)

definitions.signature: static func _polar(bearing_degrees: float, radius: float, y: float) -> Vector3:
definitions.formula: angle = deg_to_rad(bearing_degrees); return Vector3(sin(angle) * radius, y, cos(angle) * radius)
definitions.note: Parameter renamed bearing->bearing_degrees but the formula and return type are otherwise identical to Group A; the task's own instruction says cosmetic parameter-name differences don't break the grouping.

definitions.signature: static func _polar(bearing_degrees: float, radius: float, y: float) -> Vector3:
definitions.formula: angle = deg_to_rad(bearing_degrees + BEARING_SHIFT); return Vector3(sin(angle) * radius, y, cos(angle) * radius)
definitions.why_distinct: Adds a BEARING_SHIFT offset to the angle before conversion -- the same signature and return type as Group A, but a different formula.

definitions.signature: static func _polar(centre_x: float, centre_z: float, bearing: float, radius: float) -> Vector2:
definitions.formula: angle = deg_to_rad(bearing); return Vector2(centre_x + sin(angle) * radius, centre_z + cos(angle) * radius)
definitions.why_distinct: Different signature entirely (4 params, not 3), different return type (Vector2, not Vector3), computes a position relative to an explicit centre rather than the world origin.
